title: Table

ports.note: Every port a table can show, on every table, whatever its parameters say. The ports used to vary with an inputMode parameter -- reasoningInput, polygonInput and a table mode were three separate declarations of that -- so the port a connection needed might not exist on the node. Which renderer shows is now read from what is wired: src/core.ts#shownMode. The same change map_output took at 0.15.0.

ontology.note: TableView activity is implemented; broader table artifact contracts remain open. `emits` records what the module named in implementation.definition asserts, and this widget is defined in src/core.ts#TYPES, which asserts nothing — the fw:TableView facts are built in the execution case and are gated by validate:ontology-coupling, which holds at zero undeclared. Same shape as map_output 0.15.0.

changes.description: Declare every port always, and read the renderer from the connections rather than from an inputMode parameter. A practitioner could not connect Relate a column to a freshly added table: it defaulted to points, so the table port did not exist on the node. This is the direction a-map-has-layers-not-modes (2026-10-14, “there is no such thing as mode, only layers”), which was built for map_output on 2026-10-15 and left here for twelve days. The stored inputMode is still read as a fallback so a saved workflow opens showing what it showed; nothing writes it any more. A table now insists on no input at all, as a map already did: a view with nothing wired is unfinished, not failed.

evidence.note: Repository regression coverage exists; this release entry does not certify a widget independently.
